Iran War Updates: U.S. reduces troop footprint in Mideast as indirect talks with Iran continue (CBS News live, updated October 22, 2026)

Death toll rises in Saudi airport attack
Saudi authorities confirmed two deaths from the strike on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam. The General Authority of Civil Aviation stated: "The number of deaths resulting from the attack has risen to two" and identified the deceased as a Saudi citizen and Indian resident, with eight others injured.

U.S. reduces military presence
The U.S. military has quietly reduced its footprint at Middle East posts due to threats from Iran and Houthi allies. U.S. Central Command stated: "We regularly move U.S. service members and assets to optimize mission" readiness while declining operational details.

State Department orders evacuations
Non-essential U.S. embassy personnel and families must depart Saudi Arabia. State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott noted: "Iranian-supported Houthis have increasingly engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia."

Diplomatic talks continue
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi reported ongoing indirect negotiations over a seven-day ceasefire proposal, stating: "The negotiating table remains in place. It is the American side that is closing the path."

Iran threatens infrastructure targets
Revolutionary Guard official Brig. Gen. Yadollah Javani warned Iran would target undersea internet cables in the Strait of Hormuz if attacked, declaring they could "easily destroy their investments and assets."

Trump weighs military options
President Trump stated: "We just have to make a final decision of which way do we want to win?"

(Search-result summary, same outlet:) Explosions heard in Iran's Sirik port, reportedly caused by a U.S. military strike. IRGC reported four ships hit during oil transfers and three more struck mines. State Department: will continue to pressure Tehran "as long as Iran devotes its energy revenues to financing attacks on our allies, supporting terrorism around the world, and pursuing other destabilizing actions."
